payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: pass: The mug is visibly to the right of the headphones. fail: The mug is visibly not to the right of the headphones. unknown: Their relative positions cannot be determined from the image.
node.binding: Inspect the edited image and compare the mug’s position with the headphones; this directly tests the requested outcome.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.

fulfillment: The node overclaims completion: the edited image shows multiple mug-like objects and a blurred blue remnant, so the target mug’s identity and its displacement from the source are ambiguous. The trace’s “mug is right” observation alone cannot establish that the original mug was moved; it may reflect a duplicate or altered scene. Make the binding explicitly track the source mug and headphones across both images, and require the decision to reconcile final relative position with comparative evidence of progress. Treat conflicting/ambiguous object correspondence as unknown rather than yes or no; distinguish that visual uncertainty from execution or dependency failures. The reference label is aggregate guidance, not proof of a particular atomic interpretation.
s2: The node asks only whether relative position changed, so it can mark progress from a mug appearing to the headphones’ right without establishing that the original mug was moved. Bind the comparison to the source mug’s distinctive appearance and the same headphones in both images; assess correspondence and displacement, not merely the presence of any mug on the right. Here the edited image contains multiple mug-like objects and a blurred blue remnant where the source mug was, making identity and movement ambiguous despite the right-side mug. Make ambiguous or conflicting correspondence unknown, and keep that visual uncertainty distinct from execution/dependency failures. Preserve the progress criterion: do not require full completion at this node or infer an atomic answer from the aggregate partial label.

The edited image shows a blurred blue remnant at the source location, a pale mug near the headphones, and another mug to their right, so identity and movement are ambiguous; do not treat the rightmost mug alone as proof or infer a definite failure. Represent unresolved visual correspondence as unknown, distinct from execution/dependency errors. Keep this as a progress check—not a demand for full completion—and do not use the aggregate partial label as atomic ground truth."}
